Card.name: Ed Hyder's Mediterranean Marketplace
Card.description:
Family Owned and Operated Since 1975

In 1975, after working in his family’s butcher shop for many years, Ed Hyder left Grafton Hill and opened up a new 300 square foot shop on Park Avenue. He began by catering to his friends and neighbors in the Armenian, Greek, and Middle Eastern communities of Worcester; bringing them traditional foods from their native lands.

Four decades and four locations later, his children Miriam and Greg continue his legacy at 408 Pleasant St.  What started out as a tiny storefront now offers groceries and prepared foods from all over the globe,  a variety of local goods and the most unique and exciting wine selection in Worcester.

Card.name: Worcester Art Museum
Card.description:
The Worcester Art Museum connects people, communities, and cultures through the experience of art.



Our wide-ranging exhibitions tell global stories—from art made thousands of years ago to works being created today. The Museum’s collection of nearly 40,000 objects, assembled since its opening in 1898, provides a foundation to connect visitors of all ages with art, artists, and the ideas they spark. With strong ties to both our local community and the international art world, the Worcester Art Museum is an essential cultural venue for Central Massachusetts and beyond.

Card.name: Worcester Public Market
Card.description:
The Worcester Public Market is a multi-vendor, food-oriented marketplace in the European tradition, featuring street-oriented business of various stripes, a small-merchant market floor, the foodie-heaven Market Pantry, and a vibrant dining pavilion with skylights and a seamless connection to the social and gustatory pleasures of the Wachusett Brew Yard.

Located in Worcester’s resurgent Canal District, the market sits right on legendary Kelley Square, just a few seconds from Interstate 290 and a world away from the ordinary. Parking is abundant, and street life abounds. The district is home to the adjacent, mixed-use Crompton Building and offers visitors literally dozens of restaurants, bars, and eclectic retail establishments. Daytime shopping pleasures and abundant night life characterize an historic neighborhood that is undergoing a 21st century urban renaissance.

Card.name: Worcester County Poetry Association
Card.description:
The Worcester County Poetry Association is a 501(c)(3) organization funded through membership fees, publication sales, grants and donations. WCPA receives organizational support from the Massachusetts Cultural Council and has received generous programming support from the National Endowment for the Arts, Massachusetts Foundation for the Humanities, Greater Worcester Community Foundation, Worcester Cultural Commission, and Massachusetts Cultural Council, among other organizations and private donors.

The mission of the Worcester County Poetry Association is to:

Celebrate the rich literary history and creative energy of Central Massachusetts through public readings, workshops, festivals, scholarly conferences, and other programs.
Publish the literary journals The Worcester Review & ThreeDecker.
Support literary organizations in Central Massachusetts, such as The Worcester Writers' Collective, New Dawn Writers Group, The Openest Mic, The Slightly Off-Beat Writers, and more!
Collaborate with libraries, bookstores, colleges and universities, museums, churches, schools, community centers, businesses, and cultural organizations to promote poetry events.

Card.name: BirchTree Bread Company
Card.description:
Birch Tree Bread Company and Crust Bakeshop both opened in Worcester in 2014, enriching the community we love so much. Alexis began working at Crust in 2014 as a baker, and although Nate worked next door at Armsby Abbey since 2015, they truly began working together full-time at Crust in 2018, a year after Alexis purchased the bakery.

Both Alexis and Nate trained in culinary school and have collectively spent over four decades in restaurants and kitchens. Their shared passion for food shines through in every handcrafted meal, spreading joy, love, and simply delicious flavors to every guest.

From the moment they discovered Birch Tree was for sale in 2021—just after welcoming their second child—they felt like this was finally their opportunity to move forward in pursuing a long-held dream of opening a restaurant. The last three years have been filled with challenges, growth, and countless learning experiences, but they wouldn’t trade a single moment.

Two things remain true about Birch Tree. First, the food is unparalleled. Every dish is made from scratch, from  breads baked fresh daily and hand-cut fries to house-made salad dressings and creamy aiolis—you can taste the love and care in every bite. Second, the space itself, “the Tree,” is truly special. Over the years, it has hosted weddings, bridal showers, birthday parties, retirement lunches, friends reuniting, and everyday gatherings. It’s perfect for families, remote work, dates, or simply enjoying a beautiful meal in a welcoming atmosphere.

Every day, Alexis and Nate walk into the space feeling grateful for the opportunity to carry on the traditions Rob and Avra began in 2014. They are proud to serve the Worcester community with food made from the heart, and they can’t wait to feed you.

Card.name: Antonio’s Pizza By The Slice Kitchen & Bar
Card.description:
Antonio’s Pizza first opened up in 1991 in Amherst, MA to serve the vast amount of college students in what is known as the five college area. We quickly realized however, that it was not just college students that where falling in love with our pie, but the entire community (young and old). 

We quickly developed a tremendous reputation for excellent and unique pizza, efficient service and our equally unique and friendly staff. As evidenced by being voted “Best Pizza” for 21 consecutive years by the readers of the Springfield newspaper the Advocate.

After establishing ourselves as a staple in the Amherst community, the company began to explore the possibilities of expanding the Antonio’s brand of creativity, quality of product, and energy. In 2002, we opened our second restaurant in Providence, Rhode Island. Followed by additional locations in Texas, Illinois, Massachusetts and Rhode Island. With our constantly improving menu and tradition of friendly and efficient service, we were able to repeat the same success we had in Amherst. We were quickly named Best in Rhode Island by Providence Monthly. We were also featured on the Phantom Gourmet as a “Hidden Jewel.” Most recently, Antonio’s Pizza was praised as being “an amazing by-the-slice emporium” in the Providence Journal. This sort of success is what fuels our engine to grow.

CardModification.name: Antonio’s Pizza By The Slice Kitchen & Bar
CardModification.description:
Antonio’s Pizza first opened up in 1991 in Amherst, MA to serve the vast amount of college students in what is known as the five college area. We quickly realized however, that it was not just college students that where falling in love with our pie, but the entire community (young and old). 

We quickly developed a tremendous reputation for excellent and unique pizza, efficient service and our equally unique and friendly staff. As evidenced by being voted “Best Pizza” for 21 consecutive years by the readers of the Springfield newspaper the Advocate.

After establishing ourselves as a staple in the Amherst community, the company began to explore the possibilities of expanding the Antonio’s brand of creativity, quality of product, and energy. In 2002, we opened our second restaurant in Providence, Rhode Island. Followed by additional locations in Texas, Illinois, Massachusetts and Rhode Island. With our constantly improving menu and tradition of friendly and efficient service, we were able to repeat the same success we had in Amherst. We were quickly named Best in Rhode Island by Providence Monthly. We were also featured on the Phantom Gourmet as a “Hidden Jewel.” Most recently, Antonio’s Pizza was praised as being “an amazing by-the-slice emporium” in the Providence Journal. This sort of success is what fuels our engine to grow.

cards.name: BirchTree Bread Company
cards.description:
Birch Tree Bread Company and Crust Bakeshop both opened in Worcester in 2014, enriching the community we love so much. Alexis began working at Crust in 2014 as a baker, and although Nate worked next door at Armsby Abbey since 2015, they truly began working together full-time at Crust in 2018, a year after Alexis purchased the bakery.

Both Alexis and Nate trained in culinary school and have collectively spent over four decades in restaurants and kitchens. Their shared passion for food shines through in every handcrafted meal, spreading joy, love, and simply delicious flavors to every guest.

From the moment they discovered Birch Tree was for sale in 2021—just after welcoming their second child—they felt like this was finally their opportunity to move forward in pursuing a long-held dream of opening a restaurant. The last three years have been filled with challenges, growth, and countless learning experiences, but they wouldn’t trade a single moment.

Two things remain true about Birch Tree. First, the food is unparalleled. Every dish is made from scratch, from  breads baked fresh daily and hand-cut fries to house-made salad dressings and creamy aiolis—you can taste the love and care in every bite. Second, the space itself, “the Tree,” is truly special. Over the years, it has hosted weddings, bridal showers, birthday parties, retirement lunches, friends reuniting, and everyday gatherings. It’s perfect for families, remote work, dates, or simply enjoying a beautiful meal in a welcoming atmosphere.

Every day, Alexis and Nate walk into the space feeling grateful for the opportunity to carry on the traditions Rob and Avra began in 2014. They are proud to serve the Worcester community with food made from the heart, and they can’t wait to feed you.

cards.name: Worcester Art Museum
cards.description:
The Worcester Art Museum connects people, communities, and cultures through the experience of art.



Our wide-ranging exhibitions tell global stories—from art made thousands of years ago to works being created today. The Museum’s collection of nearly 40,000 objects, assembled since its opening in 1898, provides a foundation to connect visitors of all ages with art, artists, and the ideas they spark. With strong ties to both our local community and the international art world, the Worcester Art Museum is an essential cultural venue for Central Massachusetts and beyond.

cards.name: Baba Sushi
cards.description:
Step into Baba Sushi and immerse yourself in an ambiance of allure and sophistication enveloped in modern Asian décor and eclectic music. Feel the vibrant energy of a space that is both cozy and unassuming, yet seductive. Relish in the freshest, most innovative, mouth-watering sushi dishes crafted to perfection. Experience our modern and hip bar, choosing from our extensive selection of sakes or sipping on meticulously crafted specialty martinis. Baba Sushi offers a total sensory feast.

In just one year, Wilson Wang has transformed a quaint, unassuming locale into a trendy haven for modern Japanese cuisine. By melding the finest, freshest, and most innovative cuisine with a hip, sophisticated atmosphere and superior, friendly service, Wilson Wang has established a dining experience that is unparalleled in its excellence. Despite his success, Baba Sushi’s master chef and owner, Wilson Wang, renowned for his unwavering commitment to creativity and quality, continues to strive for more.
